written: 2026-09-29, before any live session of this study ran
question: In recurring-workflow tasks (same procedure, different specifics, same repository), does learning from earlier sessions of the family produce large savings on later ones?

families: click-type (10 variants: add click.<NAME> parameter type + export + API docs + guide + changelog + tests)
mm-validator (10 variants: add marshmallow.validate.<Name> + conventions + docstring + changelog + tests)
design.order: fixed in families.py before running; the first 4 of each family are training (no hooks, 1 repeat)
design.held_out: variants 5-10 of each family (12 variants), 2 repeats, arms control / adage / card, arm order seeded per (variant, repeat)

arms.adage: current target/debug/adage, `adage condition --demo` over the 4 training transcripts (+ outcomes), directives delivered
arms.card: control's hooks + the procedure card learned by procedure.py from the same 4 training transcripts, committed as CLAUDE.md (runner's agents-md slot)

primary_metric: billed $ per session (total_cost_usd), ratio arm/control - 1 over held-out sessions paired by (variant, repeat); 90% percentile bootstrap clustered by variant (12 clusters), both families pooled; also per family
secondary: tool calls per session (same ratio and CI)
pass rate (hidden check = whole test suite incl. the hidden variant check; Wilson CI per arm, paired difference)
offline: per-session decomposition into repeated-procedure calls vs novel calls (leave-one-session-out: an action is procedural if its abstract form occurs in >= half of the family's other sessions), share of calls and of $ (cumulative-context cost model)

oracle ceiling: remove every call outside the minimal path (one read + edits of each file finally changed, one passing test run); realistic ceiling: remove searches/listings and failures that repeat an earlier session's failure
learning curve: realistic removable share vs number of prior sessions n = 1..9 (random prior subsets, leave-one-out), and live points n = 0 (control) and n = 4 (card, adage)

thresholds.large: card saves >= 15% of $ with the 90% CI lower bound > 0
thresholds.adage_prediction: current adage within +-5% of control (the RepoBench finding)
thresholds.pass_rate: non-inferiority only: card must not lose more than 1 in 6 held-out variant-repeats relative to control

optional_stage: if budget remains: card learned from n = 1 prior session on the same held-out variants (1 repeat) as a second live point on the learning curve
